methods.label: Track how each pass changes the survivors
methods.explanation:
Each pass crosses out the first, third, fifth, and subsequent odd-numbered positions of the current list. It keeps exactly the even-numbered positions.

If the current list is \(d,2d,3d,\ldots\), containing all positive multiples of \(d\) up to \(100\), the next pass keeps exactly \(2d,4d,6d,\ldots\) up to \(100\). Thus each pass doubles the spacing, and this description includes every survivor.

Starting with \(d=1\), the first four passes leave all multiples of \(2\), then \(4\), then \(8\), then \(16\), respectively. After the fourth pass, the complete list is
\[
16,\ 32,\ 48,\ 64,\ 80,\ 96.
\]
The fifth pass leaves \(32,64,96\). On the sixth pass, Josh crosses out \(32\), skips \(64\), and crosses out \(96\). Exactly one number remains: \(64\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The method uses positional counting, odd and even positions, and repeated doubling. It requires neither a general sequence formula nor formal induction.
